newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Germany's Siemens in Sofia airport project.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Siemens in Sofia airport project.

text.p: Germany's Siemens AG has acquired a 50.8 percent stake in a new venture for the reconstruction of Sofia airport, Sofia City Council said on Thursday.

At its general meeting the shareholders of the venture named Sofia Airport Development Venture decided to raise its capital to 114 million levs ($62,600) from 56 million, the council said in a statement carried by state news agency BTA.
All the new shares will be bought by Siemens, which will thus acquire 50.8 percent, the statement said.

The venture, set up by Sofia Airport and Bulgarian construction company Glavbolgarstroy, will bid to carry out the 56-year-old airport's reconstruction, planned to start this autumn (October or November).
Last week Sofia City Council bought a 17 percent stake worth 9.5 million levs from Glavbolgarstroy.

The first stage of the work includes enlarging a passenger terminal to handle 3.5 million passengers per year and lengthening the runway, and is expected to cost some $120 million. Another $20-25 million will be needed for a cargo terminal to handle up to 60,000 tonnes per year.

Bulgaria hopes to receive a 60 million Ecu ($65.2 million) loan from the European Investment Bank, 25 million Ecu ($27 million) from the European Union's Phare programme and a $40-$50 million loan from the Kuwaiti Development Fund.
-- Liliana Semerdjieva, Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-91188 ($ = 0.920 European Currency Unit ECUs) ($ = 1821 Bulgarian Levs)
